correctness.rationale: The stated action is target-color rotation, not source rotation; it is geometrically free because any fixed cell would have each nonempty color subset invariant under a five-cycle. The source-coordinate forgetting map to Schultz’s smaller model commutes with target relabeling and is an underlying homotopy equivalence. Both free G-CW spaces give a G-homotopy equivalence via equivariant Whitehead. Schultz’s explicit color-subset poset identification realizes the reduced model as the boundary of an invariant derived regular neighborhood of the diagonal in M×M for M=boundary simplex. Free quotient of this derived neighborhood is a regular neighborhood of diagonal M/G in (M×M)/G, with normal bundle T(M/G), so its boundary is homotopy equivalent to S(T(M/G)). The sum-zero real C5 representation has eigenweights 1 and 2; M/G=L(5;1,2). Oriented 3-manifold parallelizability gives S(T(M/G))=S2×L(5;1,2). The Künneth homology and π1 agree with the claim. Exact independent finite orbit enumeration checks 45,540 original cells, 9,108 fivefold orbits, and χ=0; numerical checks are not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Actual published-finding corpus searches returned a same-object rational joint-character result and a full source-dihedral integral quotient. Their complete public result statements were inspected, and neither implies the target-color C5 geometric quotient homotopy equivalence. Schultz provides a natural reduced model but states a nonequivariant Stiefel homeomorphism, not this quotient lens-space product. The new consequence requires equivariant Whitehead and descending the derived regular neighborhood to the normal sphere bundle of a lens-space diagonal. Literature and database searches found no equivalent claim; implicit or unindexed publication remains a risk.

value.rationale: This is an integral homotopy classification of the first simply connected pentagon graph-coloring manifold under the natural transitive cyclic permutation of its target colors. It explains a specific lens-space factor and degree-one and degree-three five-primary torsion created by a free group action on a torsion-free manifold. The product type controls all homotopy and cohomology information for this exact canonical quotient, improving substantially on rational characters and finite counts. No arbitrary parameter slice or merely routine renaming is the point.
